topic: Shifted exponential with two unknown constants
problem: A function is defined by f(x)=a(3)^(x+2)+b, where a and b are constants. If f(0)=29 and f(1)=83, what is f(2)?

bad.why: Building 9a+b=29 and 27a+b=83 and solving by hand is a multi-step derivation the regression does instantly.
A plain y~ab^x fit ignores the +b shift and the x+2 exponent, so it fits the wrong family and gives a wrong f(2).

algebraFirst.description: Substitutes x=0 and x=1 to get 9a+b=29 and 27a+b=83, subtracts to get a=3, back-substitutes b=2, then computes 3(81)+2.

explanationNotes: Explain that f(0)=29 and f(1)=83 are two facts about the same function, so Desmos can find a and b at once by fitting f's formula to both with ~. Then f(2) is just the fitted function evaluated at 2; there is no need to work out powers of 3 or solve a system.
notes: Original variant of Bedrock Prep's hard 'Shifting Exponents' category. The two observations imply 9a+b=29 and 27a+b=83, hence a=3,b=2 and f(2)=245. If fitting parameters in Desmos, explain why the x-list has 0 and 1 and why the target is evaluated at x=2. Source category: https://www.bedrockprep.com/problems
